top.title: Alcaraz puts injury concerns aside to take apart Cobolli
top.description: Carlos Alcaraz has never won the season-ending ATP Finals title [Getty Images] A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz put aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages. Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday. He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win. The six-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory. "I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said. "I'm just really happy that I am getting more confident, the way I'm hitting the ball and seeing what's going on in the match. "The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow." Alcaraz is now on a 12-match winning streak and will face Ben Shelton, who he beat in the Paris Masters final last month, in Saturday's semi-finals. The winner of Friday's last match between Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe will face Alexander Zverev in the other semi-final. Alcaraz was conservative in his movement, trying to avoid sliding in and out of the corners - but rather than diminishing his game, it allowed him to produce some astonishing shot-making. Cobolli never looked as though he had the belief that he could challenge Alcaraz, and was broken in the first game of the match by a thumping return winner. Alcaraz kept the points short, hammering his forehand and backhand to all corners, and targeted Cobolli's second serve in particular. An astonishing whipped 110mph forehand winner was the highlight of the first set, which Alcaraz wrapped up with a strong service hold. Cobolli again lost his serve in the opening game of the second set and Alcaraz claimed five of the final six games to secure victory. After converting match point with another return winner, Alcaraz embraced Cobolli at the net and offered the crushed Italian a few words of support. Alcaraz has not had his serve broken once in his three group matches as he bids for a first title at the season-ending event. He and world number one Zverev have both made it through the group stages without dropping a set, while Alcaraz has not lost more than four games in a set. In the doubles, Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison reached the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 victory over Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos. The US Open champions will face fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic for a place in Sunday's final. top.title: ISS astronauts look down on the snow-capped Himalayas | Space photo of the day for Nov. 20, 2026
top.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.

top.title: Siena men's basketball turns page to Bucknell after historic 47-point loss at St. John's
top.description: St. John's Tounde Yessoufou (24) knocks the ball away from Siena's Parrish Edmond Jr. (3) during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, in the Queens borough of New York. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) (Frank Franklin II/Associated Press) Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith was ready to put one of the most lopsided losses in program history in the rearview mirror even before boarding the team bus outside Carnesecca Arena on Wednesday night. The Saints lost 119-72 to No. 13 St. John's in Queens, a 47-point margin of defeat that tied for the third-largest in 89 seasons of Siena basketball. "Definitely stuff to build on, but not one we're going to worry about or talk about much," Smith said. "We're just moving on and trying to get a win on Saturday (at Bucknell)." Smith said he believed his young players wouldn't overreact to the loss, which came against the defending Big East Conference Tournament champions, led by Hall of Fame coach Rick Pitino. "They know that was the best team we're going to play," Smith said. "I think it can roll off their back. I can try to instill the fact that you lose by 1, you lose by 60, it doesn't matter." Siena's only two bigger blowouts came at Syracuse. The Saints lost there by 52 points (144-92) to the 12th-ranked Orange on Jan. 17, 1979 and by 51 (123-72) to No. 7 Syracuse on Jan. 2, 1988. Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa, who had a team-high 16 points Wednesday, was ready to turn the page to Bucknell. "It's kind of the life of college basketball," he said. "You lose a game, you've got to play the next one. Just keep your head up and on to the next, I guess." Smith said it's easy for the score to get out of hand given that Siena (3-2) plays at one of the fastest paces in the country, which didn't faze a St. John's team that loves to press and run. "Score doesn't matter," he said. "The pace we play, you can never look at how many points we give up or even how many points we score. It doesn't matter. Are we efficient with our shots? Do we take the right ones. Are we getting a good point-per-shot?" Smith said Siena didn't do any of the three things he emphasized before the game: avoiding turnovers in live play, grabbing defensive rebounds and making shots. The Saints committed 15 turnovers that led to 29 St. John's points. The Red Storm had 16 offensive rebounds for 20 second-chance points. Siena shot 35.1% from the field and again struggled from 3-point range, shooting 9-for-35. "The third one, you can't really control," Smith said. "The first two we had more control over, and we didn't do a great job. Understand that's what we needed to do and we didn't do it." St. John surged to an 18-2 lead. However, the Red Storm only outscored Siena 39-38 the rest of the half to take a 57-40 lead into halftime. top.title: Throwback Dawg Day: Lambert, Georgia Hang 50-Plus On The HBC
top.description: September 19, 2015: Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Greyson Lambert (11) reacts after a touchdown in first half action of the South Carolina Gamecocks at Georgia Bulldogs game at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Have you ever had a moment of, ‘ok where in the world did that come from?’ If you were in Sanford Stadium the night of Sept, 20, 2015, you certainly experienced it. To say that the expectations for Greyson Lambert upon his transfer to Georgia from Virginia were cautious would be accurate. After all, how good could someone be who went elsewhere due to not winning a starting job at an ACC also-ran? And when you have outings like Lambert had in mid-September by going 11-21 passing against Vanderbilt, the common thinking was that he was in a role to support a very good running game, but not someone who could take over a game. That whole thinking sailed into the vapor and whisked itself up Baxter Hill on this night against South Carolina, when Lambert not only set an NCAA record on a 96 percent completion percentage, but his 24-of-25 night also set a Georgia record for most completed passes in a row. It all stacked up to Georgia rolling up 576 yards in a 52-20 win. And those 52 points were gratifying due to one opposing adversary: Steve Spurrier. The Head Ball Coach famously broke 50 points against Georgia in Athens and bragged about it. Not only that, but his return to college coaching at South Carolina further twisted the knife in Georgia’s back, misery worsened in a three-game losing streak against the Dawgs from 2010 to 2012. On this night, however, it was Georgia pouring it on to the tune of 576 yards. The big showing was not just Lambert. When you have a stable of running backs including two of the best in school history, the job has a degree of ease. Nick Chubb and Sony Michel each had touchdown runs in the second quarter before a five-yard toss to Malcolm Mitchell capped a 21-point second quarter after the game started 3-3. Michel got into the passing game act in the second half with two touchdowns receptions ahead of scoring runs by Chubb and Keith Marshall. Now, Georgia fans cannot officially claim this loss compelled Coach Spurrier to retire the next month after USC slumped to a 2-4 overall start. But it’s a fun assumption to claim. Go Dawgs!

top.description: NEW YORK, NY - SEPTEMBER 30: George Lombard Jr. #96 of the New York Yankees looks on from the on deck circle during the game against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by New York Yankees/Getty Images) | Getty Images Few positions, or the players manning them, have been debated as intensely as shortstop for the New York Yankees over the last several seasons. Heading into 2026, many fans hoped the club would find a way to move on from the Anthony Volpe experience. However, the club made no external moves and started the season with José Caballero slotted in at the position as the team waited for a rehabbing Volpe to return. Along the way, injuries and performance, both struggles by the incumbents and red-hot play in the minors, led the Yankees to hand the reins at shortstop over to 21-year-old George Lombard Jr. The rookie would spend August, September, and October at shortstop for the Yankees in what really is the throne of NYC. In terms of how it went, the staff here at PSA averaged out to a B-minus. In academic speak, that would mean Lombard understood the core material and performed above average, but did not master the assignment. Grade: B- 2026 Stats: 42 G, 166 PA, 23 R, 36 H, 4 2B, 1 3B, 7 HR, 22 RBI, 2 SB, .237/.285/.414, 92 OPS+, 93 wRC+, 0.4 fWAR, 1.1 bWAR. 2027 Contract Status: Pre-arbitration eligible. Before reaching the show, Lombard was on an absolute tear in the minors. Starting the season in Double-A, he hit .312 with a .971 OPS in 20 games, which earned him a ticket to Scranton. Lombard’s season looked like it might be coming off the rails after an adjustment period, and then he sprained two fingers, which sidelined him for a month and caused him to miss the MLB Futures Game. However, he came back in mid-July and forced the Yankees’ hand right before the Trade Deadline, going on a 14-game heater to the tune of a .377 average, .477 OBP, and 1.081 OPS. On August 4th, after surviving the Trade Deadline himself, and with the Yankees not acquiring an outside option at shortstop, the club called Lombard up to the show. top.description: ATLANTA - DECEMBER 8: Quarterback Matt Mauck #18 of the LSU Tigers falls forward during the Southeastern Conference Championship Game against the Tennessee Volunteers on December 8, 2001 at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Georgia. LSU defeated Tennessee 31-20. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the newest movie installment of “The Hunger Games” series makes its debut in theaters this week with “Sunrise on the Reaping,” my mind, when it is not on LSU lately, drifts toward how entertaining a literary and cinematic franchise it is. In some ways, it is similar to the history between LSU and Tennessee. If you have not read or seen any of the series, the brief on the story is: in a dystopian nation, the government selects one boy and one girl between the ages of 12 and 18 as tributes from each of the country’s 12 districts to enter an arena where “Gamemakers” change certain aspects of the arena while the tributes fight to the death until only one remains. The other tributes typically are not the scariest part of the arena. It is the Gamemakers sitting in a control room, randomly changing the weather, releasing bioengineered animals, supplying barbaric weaponry, and breaking your expectations the second things start looking predictable. This is what some of the Tigers’ and Volunteers’ most iconic moments together have felt like: an invisible control room hijacking the battle and rewriting expectations. LSU and Tennessee first met in 1925 in Knoxville, Tennessee, where they battled to a 0-0 tie. Since then, the Vols have held the series bragging rights with a 21-10-3 record. Tennessee strung together 10 consecutive victories from 1934 to 1959. It was almost 13, but a 3-3 tie in 1964 broke up the win streak. Since the turn of the century, LSU has dominated the series, leading 7-3 in that timeframe. “The Stop” in 1959 marked one of the most iconic moments in the history of this matchup’s early years. Riding a 19-game win streak, fresh off an SEC championship and a National championship from a season ago and a week after Heisman Trophy winner Billy Cannon’s Halloween Run against Ole Miss, No. 1 LSU led by Paul Dietzel traveled to Shields-Watkins Field in Knoxville to face No. 13 Tennessee. Late in the fourth, the Tigers would score a touchdown to cut the deficit to 14-13. They opted to go for two and the win. Who else would you give the ball to in that situation other than Cannon? Cannon would controversially be ruled short of the goal line, being stopped by Bill Majors and Wayne Grubb, effectively ending LSU’s hopes of repeating as national champions. top.title: Friday Rockpile: The legacy of Wade Davis and his impact on the Rockies
top.description: WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 25: Wade Davis #71 of the Colorado Rockies pitches during a baseball game against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on July 25, 2019 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dating back to 1871, over 23,000 people have played Major League Baseball. Of those, 281 players have been granted admission to the Baseball Hall of Fame (354 total people, including managers, pioneers, executives and umpires). It’s an elite group that includes Rockies legends Larry Walker and Todd Helton , who both were honored with statues outside of Coors Field this season. Jim Leyland, who managed the Rockies in 2024, was also elected in 2024 with Helton. The next likely candidate with a chance to get 75% of the vote is eight-time All-Star Nolan Arenado, but it will be five years after his playing days end before he is eligible. But there’s another former Rockie on this year’s ballot who deserves some praise. Wade Davis, a three-time All-Star reliever, was a member of the “super bullpen” the Rockies brought in before the 2018 season. The infamous trio didn’t live up to its billing, but Davis still had a tremendous career that’s worth recognizing. Earlier this week, Davis was named as one of 14 new players added to the ballot for the HOF class of 2027. The list is highlighted by catcher Buster Posey and pitcher Jon Lestor, but doesn’t include any runaway first-ballot inductees. They will join 13 holdovers from previous years, including Chase Utley, who earned 59.1% of the vote last year. Although he was eligible, former Rockie outfielder Dexter Fowler was left off the ballot. He’s certainly worth an honorable mention here, as he was a fan favorite, and he remains the Rockies single-season leader in triples (15 in 2011). Journeyman catcher Jonathan Lucroy, who played with the Rockies in 2017, had a distinguished 12-year career with nine teams, but also didn’t make the cut, despite being eligible. The Baseball Writers’ Association of America will fill out their ballots between now and Dec. 31, and the results will be announced on Jan. 19. The Hall of Fame Induction Weekend is slated for July 23-26. As for Davis, he was a shutdown pitcher from 2009-2017. With four years on the Tampa Bay Rays, four more with the Kansas City Royals, and another with the Chicago Cubs, the righty posted a 12.2 rWAR. Davis was a starter for his first three MLB seasons with Tampa Bay and then transitioned mostly to reliever in 2012, his last year as a Ray. nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. nigeria.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
nigeria.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
nigeria.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. nigeria.title: Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. nigeria.description: .Set to produce 6 million passports yearly By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has begun work on a centre in Abuja that will let Nigeria manufacture its own electronic passport (e-passport) booklets for the first time, with capacity to produce six million passports a year. Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Friday during the ground-breaking for the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre, at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Abuja. “The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 to 2 million passports a year, but by May, we will have the capacity for 6 million passports a year in production, which we are going to scale to 10 million booklets a year,” he said. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, broke the ground. Tunji-Ojo said the plant, which will sit on 1.1 hectares, would run off the grid and be driven by artificial intelligence. “By the time we deliver it in May, Nigeria will be the first country in West Africa to do it,” he said. He added that “there are only three countries in Africa that manufacture passports in-country”, naming South Africa, Ethiopia and Algeria. Of the three, he said, only Ethiopia has the capacity to make e-passports. The minister said the facility was not being built only for Nigeria’s needs. “What we and our partners, Iris Smart, are doing is to build a passport facility that will be able to service ECOWAS and even be able to export to other countries,” he said, referring to the Economic Community of West African States. On funding, Tunji-Ojo said the government was not footing the bill. “This project is about $70 million without a dime from government,” he said, describing Iris Smart, the vendor, as “a 100 per cent Nigerian company”. The minister disclosed that the company was first awarded an e-passport contract in 2003 under President Olusegun Obasanjo, but had been importing the booklets. He said he insisted that this must change when he assumed office. “We said we cannot be aiding employment in other countries and be creating unemployment in our own country,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said there was a heated exchange with the company over the issue. “I think the first day, I walked them out of the office. nigeria.title: Spain face France, England take on Norway in Nations League quarters
nigeria.description: World champions Spain will face France while England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League, after the draw took place on Friday. Spain beat France 2-0 in the semi-finals of the World Cup in the United States in July, on the way to winning the trophy. They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semi-finals of the last edition of the Nations League, last year. The quarter-finals will be played over two legs in late March, with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3, while France topped Group A1. Spain won the Nations League in 2023 while France beat them to win the 2021 final. England topped Group A3 on goal difference after beating Spain away in their last outing, and their reward is a two-legged last-eight tie with Norway with the first leg on Norwegian soil. England edged Norway in the World Cup quarter-finals this year before losing to Argentina in the semi-finals. The other quarter-final ties pitched reigning Nations League champions Portugal against the Netherlands, and Belgium against Germany. The winners of the quarter-finals will advance to the final stages, which will be held in June in a venue yet to be decided. Spain or France will play the Netherlands or Portugal in the semis, with England facing Belgium or Germany should they get past Norway. There will also be play-offs for relegation between Leagues A and B in late March, with Wales — who finished bottom of Group A4 — fighting for top-tier survival in a two-legged tie against Slovenia. Ireland, who came second in their group in League B, will play Croatia while Denmark face Bosnia and Herzegovina and Hungary play Serbia. The four nations already promoted to League A are Switzerland, Northern Ireland, Austria and Sweden. The Nations League quarter-finals and play-offs in March will all take place at the same time as qualifying begins for Euro 2028. nigeria.title: FIFA President Infantino Visits Warri Stadium, Pledges Support For Nigerian Football
nigeria.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended the Delta State Government for its investment in the remodelling of Warri City Stadium, describing the transformation as a significant boost to football development in Nigeria. Infantino made the remarks on Friday during an inspection visit to the stadium in Warri, Delta State, alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. He praised Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for investing in modern sports infrastructure, noting that such facilities are essential for nurturing young talents, expanding participation and creating opportunities for future generations. The FIFA president also celebrated Nigeria’s rich football heritage and its contributions to the global game, noting that some of the world’s finest footballers have emerged from the country. Infantino described the remodelled stadium as impressive, expressing enthusiasm about its facilities and his desire to play football there once the remaining work had been completed. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. ﻿ Expressing delight at the passion for football in Nigeria, Infantino said he was impressed by the energy and investment in the sport in Delta State. “It has been, and it is, really fantastic. I’m having a great time here. I can feel the love and the energy for football. This is Nigeria. This is Delta State. This is Warri. This is what we are all about. “This is heartbeat. It’s passion. It’s love, but it’s also investment. It is believing in the youth. It is believing in the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. He further applauded the recent triumph of Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing the achievement as a source of pride for Nigeria, Africa and the global football community. Referring to the Flamingos’ triumph in Morocco, he added, “The girls, they were just crowned world champions two weeks ago in Morocco. This is what we believe in. The boys and the girls. The future. The investment.” He congratulated the state government and other stakeholders on the project, assuring Nigeria of FIFA’s continued support. “So I’m very happy to be here. Congratulations to all of you. Thank you for everything you have done. You will always count on FIFA and on the FIFA president as your not just partner, but your family member. Thank you so much,” he said. Earlier, the FIFA president inaugurated the Hussey College Sports Complex in Warri, a grassroots sports facility donated by the Brownhill Foundation with support from the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board. business.title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases. The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29. Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period. “Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy. Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73. Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent. Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days. The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest. Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars. A push for a de minimis bitcoin exemption Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said. A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%. Consumers pointed to friction, too. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday. The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater. The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price. What the realized price measures Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market. The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost. The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report. “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.” Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July. Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Themed “ Celebrating the Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the evening honoured young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. Together, the five hosts gave the anniversary celebration a distinctly continental presence. Bringing different voices, personalities and perspectives to the proceedings, the line-up reflected the reach of an awards platform whose story has grown alongside the generations of young Africans it recognises. The hosts also shared the spotlight with Infinity , an AI assistant that introduced another dimension to the evening. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. sports.title: Alcaraz puts injury concerns aside to take apart Cobolli
sports.description: Carlos Alcaraz has never won the season-ending ATP Finals title [Getty Images] A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz put aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages. Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday. He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win. The six-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory. "I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said. "I'm just really happy that I am getting more confident, the way I'm hitting the ball and seeing what's going on in the match. "The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow." Alcaraz is now on a 12-match winning streak and will face Ben Shelton, who he beat in the Paris Masters final last month, in Saturday's semi-finals. The winner of Friday's last match between Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe will face Alexander Zverev in the other semi-final. Alcaraz was conservative in his movement, trying to avoid sliding in and out of the corners - but rather than diminishing his game, it allowed him to produce some astonishing shot-making. Cobolli never looked as though he had the belief that he could challenge Alcaraz, and was broken in the first game of the match by a thumping return winner. Alcaraz kept the points short, hammering his forehand and backhand to all corners, and targeted Cobolli's second serve in particular. An astonishing whipped 110mph forehand winner was the highlight of the first set, which Alcaraz wrapped up with a strong service hold. Cobolli again lost his serve in the opening game of the second set and Alcaraz claimed five of the final six games to secure victory. After converting match point with another return winner, Alcaraz embraced Cobolli at the net and offered the crushed Italian a few words of support. Alcaraz has not had his serve broken once in his three group matches as he bids for a first title at the season-ending event. He and world number one Zverev have both made it through the group stages without dropping a set, while Alcaraz has not lost more than four games in a set. In the doubles, Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison reached the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 victory over Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos. Smith said he believed his young players wouldn't overreact to the loss, which came against the defending Big East Conference Tournament champions, led by Hall of Fame coach Rick Pitino. "They know that was the best team we're going to play," Smith said. "I think it can roll off their back. I can try to instill the fact that you lose by 1, you lose by 60, it doesn't matter." Siena's only two bigger blowouts came at Syracuse. The Saints lost there by 52 points (144-92) to the 12th-ranked Orange on Jan. 17, 1979 and by 51 (123-72) to No. 7 Syracuse on Jan. 2, 1988. Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa, who had a team-high 16 points Wednesday, was ready to turn the page to Bucknell. "It's kind of the life of college basketball," he said. Smith said it's easy for the score to get out of hand given that Siena (3-2) plays at one of the fastest paces in the country, which didn't faze a St. John's team that loves to press and run. "Score doesn't matter," he said. "The pace we play, you can never look at how many points we give up or even how many points we score. It doesn't matter. Are we efficient with our shots? Smith said Siena didn't do any of the three things he emphasized before the game: avoiding turnovers in live play, grabbing defensive rebounds and making shots. sports.description: September 19, 2015: Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Greyson Lambert (11) reacts after a touchdown in first half action of the South Carolina Gamecocks at Georgia Bulldogs game at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Have you ever had a moment of, ‘ok where in the world did that come from?’ If you were in Sanford Stadium the night of Sept, 20, 2015, you certainly experienced it. To say that the expectations for Greyson Lambert upon his transfer to Georgia from Virginia were cautious would be accurate. After all, how good could someone be who went elsewhere due to not winning a starting job at an ACC also-ran? And when you have outings like Lambert had in mid-September by going 11-21 passing against Vanderbilt, the common thinking was that he was in a role to support a very good running game, but not someone who could take over a game. That whole thinking sailed into the vapor and whisked itself up Baxter Hill on this night against South Carolina, when Lambert not only set an NCAA record on a 96 percent completion percentage, but his 24-of-25 night also set a Georgia record for most completed passes in a row. It all stacked up to Georgia rolling up 576 yards in a 52-20 win. And those 52 points were gratifying due to one opposing adversary: Steve Spurrier. The Head Ball Coach famously broke 50 points against Georgia in Athens and bragged about it. Not only that, but his return to college coaching at South Carolina further twisted the knife in Georgia’s back, misery worsened in a three-game losing streak against the Dawgs from 2010 to 2012. On this night, however, it was Georgia pouring it on to the tune of 576 yards. The big showing was not just Lambert. When you have a stable of running backs including two of the best in school history, the job has a degree of ease. Nick Chubb and Sony Michel each had touchdown runs in the second quarter before a five-yard toss to Malcolm Mitchell capped a 21-point second quarter after the game started 3-3. Michel got into the passing game act in the second half with two touchdowns receptions ahead of scoring runs by Chubb and Keith Marshall. Now, Georgia fans cannot officially claim this loss compelled Coach Spurrier to retire the next month after USC slumped to a 2-4 overall start. But it’s a fun assumption to claim. Go Dawgs!

sports.description: We’re getting closer to Mauricio Pochettino taking charge of his first game as head coach of Manchester United. The Argentinian is still with the United States national team at present, concluding a two-legged CONCACAF Nations League meeting with Haiti – the first game of which was last night – and is due to start work with the Reds on 18 November. Just a few short days later comes his first game in charge, and it’s a big one: a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool. Bryan Mbeumo – our joint-top scorer in the Premier League this season on four, tied with Fernandes – also scored in that game, with Maguire’s winner cancelling out a Cody Gakpo leveller. He later took the top job at Tottenham Hotspur, who he registered consistent top-four finishes with, while taking them to the UEFA Champions League final in 2019. Stints at some of Europe’s biggest clubs in Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea followed, before he crossed the Atlantic to lead the Stars and Stripes into their home FIFA World Cup over the summer. sports.description: ATLANTA - DECEMBER 8: Quarterback Matt Mauck #18 of the LSU Tigers falls forward during the Southeastern Conference Championship Game against the Tennessee Volunteers on December 8, 2001 at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Georgia. LSU defeated Tennessee 31-20. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the newest movie installment of “The Hunger Games” series makes its debut in theaters this week with “Sunrise on the Reaping,” my mind, when it is not on LSU lately, drifts toward how entertaining a literary and cinematic franchise it is. In some ways, it is similar to the history between LSU and Tennessee. If you have not read or seen any of the series, the brief on the story is: in a dystopian nation, the government selects one boy and one girl between the ages of 12 and 18 as tributes from each of the country’s 12 districts to enter an arena where “Gamemakers” change certain aspects of the arena while the tributes fight to the death until only one remains. The other tributes typically are not the scariest part of the arena. It is the Gamemakers sitting in a control room, randomly changing the weather, releasing bioengineered animals, supplying barbaric weaponry, and breaking your expectations the second things start looking predictable. This is what some of the Tigers’ and Volunteers’ most iconic moments together have felt like: an invisible control room hijacking the battle and rewriting expectations. LSU and Tennessee first met in 1925 in Knoxville, Tennessee, where they battled to a 0-0 tie. Since then, the Vols have held the series bragging rights with a 21-10-3 record. Tennessee strung together 10 consecutive victories from 1934 to 1959. It was almost 13, but a 3-3 tie in 1964 broke up the win streak. Since the turn of the century, LSU has dominated the series, leading 7-3 in that timeframe. “The Stop” in 1959 marked one of the most iconic moments in the history of this matchup’s early years. Riding a 19-game win streak, fresh off an SEC championship and a National championship from a season ago and a week after Heisman Trophy winner Billy Cannon’s Halloween Run against Ole Miss, No. 1 LSU led by Paul Dietzel traveled to Shields-Watkins Field in Knoxville to face No. 13 Tennessee. Late in the fourth, the Tigers would score a touchdown to cut the deficit to 14-13. They opted to go for two and the win. Who else would you give the ball to in that situation other than Cannon? Cannon would controversially be ruled short of the goal line, being stopped by Bill Majors and Wayne Grubb, effectively ending LSU’s hopes of repeating as national champions. The legend of Matt Mauck started in 2001 with another unexpected twist in the series. No. 2 Tennessee, with a 10-1 record, had already beaten LSU earlier in the season in Knoxville, 26-18, and marched into Atlanta for the SEC championship game for a rematch against the Tigers. sports.description: WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 25: Wade Davis #71 of the Colorado Rockies pitches during a baseball game against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on July 25, 2019 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dating back to 1871, over 23,000 people have played Major League Baseball. Of those, 281 players have been granted admission to the Baseball Hall of Fame (354 total people, including managers, pioneers, executives and umpires). It’s an elite group that includes Rockies legends Larry Walker and Todd Helton , who both were honored with statues outside of Coors Field this season. Jim Leyland, who managed the Rockies in 2024, was also elected in 2024 with Helton. The next likely candidate with a chance to get 75% of the vote is eight-time All-Star Nolan Arenado, but it will be five years after his playing days end before he is eligible. But there’s another former Rockie on this year’s ballot who deserves some praise. Wade Davis, a three-time All-Star reliever, was a member of the “super bullpen” the Rockies brought in before the 2018 season. The infamous trio didn’t live up to its billing, but Davis still had a tremendous career that’s worth recognizing. Earlier this week, Davis was named as one of 14 new players added to the ballot for the HOF class of 2027. The list is highlighted by catcher Buster Posey and pitcher Jon Lestor, but doesn’t include any runaway first-ballot inductees. They will join 13 holdovers from previous years, including Chase Utley, who earned 59.1% of the vote last year. Although he was eligible, former Rockie outfielder Dexter Fowler was left off the ballot. He’s certainly worth an honorable mention here, as he was a fan favorite, and he remains the Rockies single-season leader in triples (15 in 2011). Journeyman catcher Jonathan Lucroy, who played with the Rockies in 2017, had a distinguished 12-year career with nine teams, but also didn’t make the cut, despite being eligible. The Baseball Writers’ Association of America will fill out their ballots between now and Dec. 31, and the results will be announced on Jan. 19. The Hall of Fame Induction Weekend is slated for July 23-26. As for Davis, he was a shutdown pitcher from 2009-2017. With four years on the Tampa Bay Rays, four more with the Kansas City Royals, and another with the Chicago Cubs, the righty posted a 12.2 rWAR. In 393 appearances, including 88 starts, he posted a 3.45 ERA with two complete games, 79 saves, 768 strikeouts and a 59-39 record. Davis was a starter for his first three MLB seasons with Tampa Bay and then transitioned mostly to reliever in 2012, his last year as a Ray. That season, he made 54 appearances out of the bullpen, posting a 2.43 ERA in 70.1 innings. After All-Star nods for three straight years (2015-2017) and winning a World Series with the Royals in 2015, Davis established himself as one of the most dominant relievers in the game. sports.title: Old connections, new roles: The coaching history behind Bills vs. Dolphins
sports.description: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. Kelly and the Bills made four consecutive Super Bowl appearances while Marino never returned after his lone trip following the 1984 season. These days, the rivalry belongs mostly to Buffalo. Since Josh Allen arrived in Western New York in 2018, he’s gone 14–3 against Miami, including a playoff victory. The Dolphins have managed to sneak in three wins — just enough to make Allen and the rest of Bills Mafia angry before the next meeting. But the Dolphins coming to Buffalo this week look very different from the team that challenged the Bills’ hold on the AFC East just a couple of seasons ago. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle are gone. So are Minkah Fitzpatrick and Bradley Chubb, who now wears a Bills uniform. De’Von Achane is still in Miami but sidelined with an injury. And with starting quarterback Malik Willis also on injured reserve, Kyle McCord is preparing for just his second NFL start. Miami may have a new look, but that doesn’t mean everyone on its sideline is unfamiliar with Buffalo. Several members of Jeff Hafley’s coaching staff have faced the Bills in previous stops around the league, while others have crossed paths with the coaches now leading Buffalo. For this week’s Time Capsule, we’re looking beyond the players to revisit some of those coaching connections, the games they’ve been part of, and the history they’re bringing into Sunday’s matchup. _____________________________________________________________________________ Jim Leonhard vs. Kevin Patullo Buffalo defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard and Miami passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo have already been on opposite sidelines, and their last meeting didn’t end particularly well for Patullo. In October 2025, Leonhard was Denver’s assistant head coach and defensive passing game coordinator, while Patullo was running Philadelphia’s offense. The Eagles entered the game undefeated and looked ready to stay that way, building a 17–3 lead early in the third quarter. After all those primetime games, not having the Bears in action made the bye week feel longer than usual. Now the Bears kickoff a very tough, but important stretch of football. The Saints and Dolphins stand as the only two losing teams on their remaining slate. And they still have to face the gauntlet of the NFC North four more times. It starts with the Saints, though. And while their record is not good, it’s the NFL. Chicago is in no position to overlook an opponent. The Saints have talent. They’ve been in most of their games this season. In fact, all but two of their games have been decided by one score or less. So it’s no walk in the park. Our crew breaks down what it will take for Chicago to get the win on Sunday. Sam: This is the worst defense the Bears have faced in a month. However, they have a formidable pass-rushing duo in Chase Young and Chad Granderson. If the Bears slow them down, they will be able to get back to the run game we saw earlier this season. That will set up play action. For the defense, the Saints look like they’ll be without their starting RT and C. That should give the advantage to Montez Sweat and Jeffery Simmons. technology.description: Microsoft has delivered its final scheduled non-security preview update of 2026 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, with an updated Windows Search experience and a brighter Windows Hello for users who prefer darker rooms. The optional KB5132057 update arrived on November 19, after this month's Patch Tuesday. Microsoft is skipping December's non-security preview because of reduced holiday operations, though that doesn't cancel the monthly security release. This last preview is quite a doozy. The big-ticket item is the "new Windows Search Experience." We saw a preview of this last month, and Microsoft has gone well beyond the "just make it work" request of many Windows users. Results appear faster with less clutter, the tool uses memory better, and files can be previewed directly in Windows Search. We're less convinced by inline actions, which let users perform common tasks directly through Windows Search without opening Settings. In our testing, "turn on dark mode" worked, but "switch on dark mode" did not, thus highlighting the limitations of the tool. In addition, we remain unconvinced that Windows Search is the place to run actions. That said, anything that makes Windows Search less of a punchline for unkind jokes about performance and accuracy is welcome, as are other features, including an optional screen-brightening feature for Windows Hello facial recognition in dim rooms, and the PowerToys-esque Run dialog, which users can enable in Settings. While some of the new features won't be enabled immediately, Microsoft has included fixes that will be available right away. One addresses an issue where Windows Fax and Scan could fail to connect to a fax server. Handy for those occasions when email falls over into a heap . There are also fixes for Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC activation failures and the misleading "Something went wrong" message shown on Android devices during cross-device passkey authentication. At the time of writing, Microsoft still lists the problem as something for which "we are working on a resolution to be released in a future Windows update." Sadly, not everything has been pushed off the naughty step. SQL Server queries using OLE DB providers can still leave connections to external databases open after they've finished. technology.title: Microsoft suggests Registry hack to work around hotpatch woes
technology.description: Some Windows 11 applications might fail to install or launch after Microsoft's November hotpatch, but not to worry: there's a Registry tweak to work around it. Microsoft has confirmed it isn't administrators' imaginations. The November hotpatch is causing application errors, including in little-used and obscure apps such as Outlook. Affected applications may fail during installation, launch, or use, displaying errors such as " ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099) ." Microsoft's investigation points to applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. The problem is more common with 32-bit software, but can also affect 64-bit applications "under certain circumstances." The workaround involves fiddling with the Registry on affected devices, so is not for the faint of heart and a backup is a good idea before diving in. Microsoft says the key " HotPatchTableSize " in the folder " HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management " needs to be set to " 2000 " followed by a restart. Just the thing to round out the week for administrators. The issue affects the November hotpatch, not the standard monthly cumulative security update. "Devices which installed the November 2026 Windows monthly security update are not expected to be affected by this issue," Microsoft said. Windows hotpatches are security updates that don't require a device restart (unless, as in this instance, administrators have to do so to address errors after a hotpatch is installed). Windows 11 hotpatching requires version 24H2 or later, an eligible subscription, and the necessary management and security configuration. "Hotpatch update package size is significantly smaller than the standard cumulative updates," Microsoft said, and the goal is to "streamline the installation process and enhance compliance efficiency." The offending hotpatch, KB5132043 , was released on November 10. It followed the October 13 baseline , which was a prerequisite. Microsoft made hotpatching the default in Windows Autopatch earlier this year. At the time, we asked: " What could possibly go wrong? " Thanks to November's hotpatch, we have our answer. ®

Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration. Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications. Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade. Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better. For example, a survey of SAP users last year found that 95 percent said building a positive case for migration required substantial effort or was genuinely challenging. Speaking to The Register , Jennifer Colapietro, PwC digital core modernization platform leader, said: "You're seeing it a lot more as part of the rationale for the business case for why they should upgrade, answering the question: 'Why now? "Folks have budgets for ERP, but now [funding for transformation is] being split because they also have budgets for AI. But there's synergies across them. If you look at moving to a clean digital core ERP, that will help them to realize the AI value faster... be able to turn on AI and be able to start to automate a lot of the processes and implement the agents. technology.title: UK government can't keep its encryption-busting order to Apple a secret, tribunal rules
technology.description: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN), rejecting the Home Office's argument that acknowledging its existence would damage national security. The order has been widely reported as demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials, and media briefings they concluded had been authorized by the UK government. The Home Office had previously adopted its "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) policy, as is standard when discussing national security matters. The story broke in February 2025, when The Washington Post reported that the Home Office had demanded an iCloud backdoor the previous month. A TCN is a notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which compels recipients, such as tech companies, to implement technical changes that facilitate the UK government's legal surveillance powers. For Apple, a company that has long made privacy central to its marketing, and famously rejected an FBI order to break open an iPhone to assist a terror probe, being served the TCN meant it either had to somehow defy a legal order issued by the UK, or undermine the encryption technology that customers expected. While it remained officially unconfirmed at the time, Apple's decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users in February 2025 was widely interpreted as indirect confirmation of the demand. At the same time, US policymakers urged then-director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard to oppose the UK's demands under the assumption that they also sought to backdoor Apple's data in a way that would affect US citizens. In August 2025, Gabbard announced that the UK had agreed to drop its demand for access to Americans' encrypted data. ADP is still available to users in the US. Apple's ADP extends end-to-end encryption to additional categories of iCloud data, including backups, photos, and notes. Only trusted devices retain access to the relevant encryption keys, leaving Apple unable to decrypt that protected content for investigators. Without ADP, those additional categories revert to standard protection: the data remains encrypted, but Apple holds the keys and can disclose content in response to valid legal demands. Some categories remain end-to-end encrypted regardless. Apple has an explainer on what data types remain end-to-end encrypted, even without ADP enabled, and those that are not. What the judgment does not confirm While the IPT's judgment confirms that the Home Office served Apple with a TCN, judges have yet to decide whether key details about the case can be made public. technology.title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
technology.description: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2. The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again." Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored." Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID. Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected. An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets. Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057 , the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop."
